name: PT Vale Indonesia Tbk

frontmatter.title: Vale Indonesia: matte cash flow, an ore business in the making, and a licence that ends
frontmatter.summary: We initiate on PT Vale Indonesia at HOLD with a Rp3,227 target and a 1.9% total return. The shares price a matte smelter at the bottom of the nickel cycle; we also carry the ore business built at Bahodopi and Pomalaa, a cash cost held through the cycle, and a licence that runs to the middle of the century. Indonesian quota policy, not the balance sheet, is the risk.
thesis: We initiate at HOLD with a Rp3,227 target, 1.9% total return and a 12.1% WACC on a licence that ends in 2045 [S2][model].
The matte cash cost has held near US$9,339/t for two years and the first nine months of 2026 already earned US$297.0m of EBITDA against US$166.0m a year earlier [F6][F7][F27][F42].
Ore sales have become a second engine at 2.4 Mt from Bahodopi and 1.9 Mt from Pomalaa in nine months, run at a 55.7% margin and ramping with the two HPAL projects [S4][S7][S8].

The target is the life-of-licence DCF at the desk's through-cycle nickel marker, Rp3,286; the EV/EBITDA and P/BV cross-checks both capitalise a trough year or a book that earns below its cost of equity, and carry no weight [model].
Scenarios are mirrored at 25% / 50% / 25% probabilities with values of Rp670, Rp3,511 and Rp5,217 [model].
The risk that matters is Indonesian supply policy, meaning the annual RKAB, the quota the minister has said he will cut for 2027 and the smelter moratorium the ministry is studying [S10][S11].

catalysts.event: National nickel RKAB for 2027, and the quota cut the energy minister flagged in November
FY2026 results: first full year of ore revenue and the Pomalaa ramp
Annual report: reserve statement, Morowali completion and HPAL commissioning

blocks.text: We initiate coverage of PT Vale Indonesia Tbk at **HOLD** with a twelve-month target of **Rp3,227**, a 1.9% total return against the Rp3,360 price [S0]. Vale mines saprolitic nickel ore at Sorowako in South Sulawesi, smelts it into nickel matte in its own furnaces and has added a second revenue line selling ore from the Bahodopi and Pomalaa blocks [S6][S4]. The Indonesian state holds 34.0% through MIND ID following the divestment that converted the old Contract of Work into an IUPK [S2][F23].

**What the market is paying for.** On our first forecast year the shares trade at 4.8x EV/EBITDA and 10.3x P/E [model], a multiple that capitalises a matte business at the bottom of the nickel cycle and assigns very little to the ore stream, which only became material in the last year [S4]. Our method is a life-of-licence DCF at the desk's through-cycle nickel marker, discounted at a 12.1% WACC and run to FY2045E — the IUPK to 2035 plus one ten-year extension — with no terminal value; it gives Rp3,286 [model][S2 p.476][F53]. The EV/EBITDA and P/BV cross-checks are reported in the valuation section and carry no weight, because one capitalises a trough year and the other a peer premium to a book that earns below its cost of equity [model]. The target is Rp3,227 and the next-twelve-month dividend of Rp196 supplies the rest of the total return [model].

**The base case is the most likely path, not the cautious one.** We anchor FY2026E on the actual run-rate: nine-month production of 48.1 kt Ni, a third-quarter figure of 18.3 kt Ni that was the strongest of the year after the early maintenance and licensing stoppage [S4], and a fourth quarter at roughly the third-quarter rate, which gives sales of 68.5 kt of nickel in matte [model]. Realisation is 82.0% of the benchmark, the average of the first nine months, and the cash cost is US$8,760 per tonne ex-royalty, which reconciles the reported US$297.0m of nine-month EBITDA [S4][model]. On those inputs FY2026E revenue is US$1,229.9m, EBITDA US$377.1m at a 30.7% margin and net profit US$189.8m [model]. The FY2025 base was deliberately not carried forward: it was the year the ore business had barely started and the smelter ran below capacity [S2][S4].

**The two things that move the value.** The first is the nickel marker, which the desk carries at US$17,089/t for the current year and US$17,500/t long run against a spot of US$16,324/t [S0]; every tenth of the marker is worth roughly a tenth of the matte margin. The second is Indonesian supply policy: the government reinstated an annual RKAB approval mechanism for 2026, revised the domestic ore reference price formula in April 2026, and the energy minister has said he will cut the 2027 nickel quota to defend the price [S2][S10]. A tighter quota lifts the marker and the company's ore price together, which is why we shock the nickel price and the ore revenue in the same direction in both tail scenarios [model].

Nickel is mined two ways. Laterite ore is either smelted into ferronickel or nickel pig iron for
stainless steel, or leached under pressure into a hydroxide precipitate for batteries. Indonesia
dominates both routes, and its policy on how much ore may leave the ground is the single largest
influence on the world price. A producer with its own hydro power and a long licence sits at the
low-carbon, high-grade end of that industry.

Vale Indonesia is an integrated laterite miner and matte producer. It mines saprolitic ore in the Sorowako block of East Luwu, South Sulawesi, and processes it through drying, reduction and electric furnaces into nickel matte, which is sold to stainless-steel and battery supply chains rather than to the nickel pig iron route that most Indonesian tonnage feeds [S6][S2]. The smelter is powered by the company's own hydroelectric plants on the Larona river system, which have 365 MW of installed capacity and supply the operation while exporting a small surplus to the state grid [S6]. That captive hydro is why the company's power cost is not hostage to coal and why its emissions intensity is low by Indonesian nickel standards [S6].

The product mix is changing. Alongside matte, the company sells nickel ore from Bahodopi in Central Sulawesi and from Pomalaa in Southeast Sulawesi to third-party processing plants, and that stream has become material: ore sales were 2.3 Mt in FY2025 [F20] and reached 2.4 Mt from Bahodopi and 1.9 Mt from Pomalaa in the first nine months of 2026 [S4]. Matte is still the larger line. FY2025 revenue was US$990.2m, of which matte at the US$12,157/t realised price on 73.1 kt Ni of sales accounted for about nine tenths and ore the remainder [S2][F2][F5][F14]. The ore business earns a much higher margin than smelting, which is the reason the blended margin rises as ore volumes grow [S4][S0].

The growth plan is two high-pressure acid leach projects. Pomalaa is designed to produce 120 kt Ni a year in mixed hydroxide precipitate, a joint venture with Huayou and Ford, at an investment of US$4,500.0m [S7]. Morowali is designed to produce 60.0 kt Ni a year, developed with GEM and EcoPro under the BNSI joint venture, at US$2,000.0m, with the mining done by Vale and the processing by the joint venture [S8]. Pomalaa reached mechanical completion on its first two trains in the third quarter of 2026 [S4]; the Morowali autoclave arrived in July 2026 and the plant is scheduled for completion in 2027 [S8]. Both projects are fed by Vale's own ore, which is why the ore line and the project timeline are the same story [S7][S8]. Vale's economic interest in the processing ventures is smaller than the headline capacity implies: after successive dilutions it holds 5.8% of PT Kolaka Nickel Indonesia, the Pomalaa vehicle, and 26.5% of PT Bahodopi Nickel Smelting Indonesia, the Morowali vehicle, so its attributable share is under a tenth of Pomalaa's design output and about a quarter of Morowali's [S2 p.150][F51][F52]. The stakes sit on the balance sheet at US$19.9m and are carried in the equity bridge rather than valued separately [S2 p.148][F50].

Ownership is a strategic bloc plus a thin float. MIND ID holds 34.0% after the mandatory divestment, the balance sits with the original Vale and Sumitomo shareholders, and the free float is about a fifth of the shares [S2][S0]. The IUPK is a continuation of the Contract of Work and runs to 2045, which is the horizon we use for the DCF rather than the much longer reserve life [S2]. The company is a single-segment producer with no listed subsidiaries to puzzle over, so the equity is a clean read on one integrated mining and smelting operation [S2][S0].

On scale Vale is a mid-tier producer by tonnage but a high-grade one by product. Its matte carries a high nickel content that suits both stainless and battery converters, its ore is sold to plants that need exactly its chemistry, and its permits and hydro base are not replicable at short notice [S6][S7]. The moat is therefore regulatory and geological rather than commercial: the company does not set the price it is paid, it does not own the downstream plants that buy its ore, and its returns move with the marker [S2][S8].

Nickel demand is split between stainless steel, which takes the bulk of global tonnage, and batteries, which take a smaller but faster-growing share and pay for the class of ore that Vale sells [S10][S5]. Indonesia supplies the majority of the world's nickel and almost all of its growth, so the marginal tonne that sets the price is Indonesian, and the policy that governs Indonesian supply is the main swing factor for the price [S10]. That is the structural reason a single-country quota decision moves this company's earnings more than any operating variable it controls [S10][S2].

Supply policy has tightened through 2026. The government reinstated an annual work plan and budget approval, the RKAB, replacing the three-year scheme, and Vale's 2026 RKAB was approved in January after a temporary suspension of mining across its licence areas while the approval was pending [S2]. The ministry has since cut the national ore quota and revised the domestic ore reference price formula in April 2026 to make the domestic price reflect market conditions more closely [S2]. In November the energy minister said he would cut the 2027 nickel quota, citing an oversupplied world market and the success of the same approach in coal [S10]. The ministry is also studying a moratorium on new smelters that produce only semi-finished metal, which would slow the capacity growth that has pressured the price [S11].

The price. The desk carries the nickel benchmark at US$15,162/t for the last actual, US$17,089/t for the current year and US$17,500/t long run, against a spot of US$16,324/t at the end of September 2026 [S0]. The series behind the marker is the World Bank Pink Sheet (October 2026 edition) for the actuals and the World Bank Commodity Markets Outlook for the long-run anchor, a named public series rather than a vendor quote [model]. As a cross-check, the company prepared its own reserve statement at a nickel price of US$17,775/t, a level above the marker, and at a higher range again for Pomalaa — evidence that the house marker is not above what a producer would plan on [S2 p.75][F55]. The market traded below that spot at the start of November on oversupply worries and rebounded to roughly the spot level later in the same week as Indonesian enforcement tightened [S10][S5]. Our forecast uses the deck rather than the spot, because a producer with a nineteen-year licence should be valued through the cycle and the desk series is the reviewed through-cycle view [S0].

Competitive positioning. Vale sits at the high-grade, low-carbon end of the Indonesian cost curve: its matte is a premium product, its power is hydro rather than coal, and its ore is the feedstock the new leach plants need [S6][S7]. It is not a low-cost nickel pig iron producer and it does not compete on the marginal tonne; it competes on product quality and permit security. The practical peer set is the Indonesian nickel complex, including the stainless and ferronickel names we use for the multiple cross-check [model]. Five forces are mixed: buyer power is high because the marker is set elsewhere, supplier power is low, entry is barred by permits and capital, substitution comes from other nickel units, and rivalry is intensifying as Indonesian capacity grows [S10][S2].

The nickel market has two prices inside it. The London benchmark prices refined metal, while ore and
intermediate products such as matte and hydroxide trade at negotiated premiums or discounts to it,
depending on chemistry and location. A producer's realised price is therefore a policy-influenced spread
to a global marker, and the spread can move independently of the marker itself.

Revenue fell from US$1,179.5m in FY2022 to US$950.4m in FY2024 as the nickel price came off its peak, then recovered to US$990.2m in FY2025 on higher sales volume [S0][S2]. Gross profit in the last actual was US$110.9m and EBIT US$36.9m after US$73.9m of operating expense [S0]. Depreciation and amortisation was US$165.0m, a line the data pack does not carry and which we take from the accounts [F9][S2], so FY2025 EBITDA was US$201.9m at a 20.4% margin [S0]. The margin is thin because the smelter converts a commodity into a commodity, and it is the ore line that has lifted it since [S4].

Cost is the fixed point of the model. The reported unit cash cost of sales was US$9,339/t in FY2025 against US$9,374/t in FY2024, so two years of input inflation were absorbed without the cost line moving [F7][F6]. That reported figure already contains the royalty: the filing's cost of production of US$888.3m reconciles to the per-tonne cash cost on the year's volume plus depreciation plus the ore cost of sales, with the US$42.4m royalty carried as a line inside it [S2 p.159][F19][F7][F9][F18]. The model therefore carries the cash cost ex-royalty and adds the royalty at 4.3% of matte revenue, which is the rate the accounts actually paid, not a schedule read [S2][F18]. Double counting that charge would have understated EBITDA by the royalty every year.

The first nine months of 2026 are the live evidence. Revenue was US$896.0m, EBITDA US$297.0m against US$166.0m in the same period of 2025, and net profit US$147.0m [S4]. The third quarter alone earned US$353.0m of revenue on production of 18.3 kt Ni, at a realised price of US$14,053/t and a unit cash cost of US$10,404/t [S4]. The cost increase is energy: marine fuel oil consumption rose and coal consumption rose more, and both commodities cost more in the quarter [S4]. Matte shipments in the quarter were the highest of the year, which is why revenue grew faster than production [S4].

Our forecast anchors on those actuals rather than on FY2025. We carry 68.5 kt of sales for FY2026E, built from nine-month production of 48.1 kt Ni plus a fourth quarter at the third-quarter rate [S4][model], and then hold the smelter at 72.0 kt, which is the FY2025 sales rate less normal maintenance [F2]. Realisation is 82.0% of the benchmark in FY2026E, the average of the two reported quarters, and reverts to the FY2025 calibration of 80.0% from FY2027E [S4][F5][model]. The cash cost is held flat in real terms at US$8,760 per tonne ex-royalty, which is what the nine-month EBITDA implies once the ore stream is credited at its normal margin [S4][model]. Ore revenue is US$270.0m in FY2026E at a 55.7% gross margin and ramps to the capacity the two projects need by the end of the forecast [S7][S8][model]. That margin is a residual from the filing itself — ore revenue of US$101.6m less the ore cost left once the matte cash cost, depreciation and the royalty are taken out of the US$888.3m cost of production — and then reduced for the royalty the ore line itself pays, which is why it is 55.7% and not the higher figure a margin on a truncated cost base would give [S2 p.159][F19][F45][F18].

Capex is the swing in the cash flow. FY2025 capex was US$523.0m, split between sustaining spend and growth spend that was realised well below the growth budget the company had set for the year [F11][S2 p.175]. For FY2026E we carry US$546.5m in total: sustaining spend at the last-actual per-tonne rate plus the company's own US$389.0m growth target and US$179.0m sustaining target, then a declining project line as Pomalaa and Morowali complete [S2 p.179][F47][F48]. Working capital is held at 0.9% of revenue, the last-actual ratio rather than a three-year average that would book a release the last year does not show [S0]. The balance sheet is a buffer, not a lever: at the FY2025 year-end the company held US$382.2m of cash against US$3.5m of debt, and the September 2026 position was still in net cash [S0].

**Earnings-quality flags.** Cash conversion is clean: operating cash flow of US$234.7m in FY2025 exceeded net profit of US$76.1m, so earnings were cash-backed and the accrual charge was negative [F43][F15][S2]. The **depreciation restatement** is a correction rather than a flag: the pack carries no D&A line, the accounts do, and the US$165.0m charge is now in the model and in the cash flow [F9][S2]. The **royalty treatment** is disclosed in the cost basis above and is the one place our forecast differs mechanically from the reported per-tonne cost [S0][F18]. **Related-party exposure** is structural rather than abusive: MIND ID is the controlling shareholder at 34.0% and the company buys services from the Vale group, which the annual report discloses [S2][S0]. We found no special-notation or monitoring-board status and no serial equity issuance in the record we hold, which is a checked absence rather than a clean bill [S0]. The payout is 60.2% of FY2024 earnings under a stated sixty per cent policy, and the FY2025 charge is being paid out of cash the ore business is generating [S2][F17].

We value Vale with the house commodity-producer method set: a life-of-licence DCF at through-cycle prices as the primary method, cross-checked against EV/EBITDA and P/BV [config]. That is the right frame for a price-taking producer because a spot multiple capitalises whichever year the cycle happens to be in, while the licence life and the reserve stock are what a buyer actually owns [S0][S2].

The cost of capital comes from the macro deck: a risk-free rate of 4.9%, a mature-market equity premium of 4.2%, an Indonesia country premium of 2.5% and an unlevered beta of 1.10 that levers to 1.18 at the company's net cash position [S0]. With a cost of equity of 12.8% and a pre-tax cost of debt of 6.9%, the WACC is 12.1% [S0]. The debt weight is small because the balance sheet is in net cash, so the WACC is close to the cost of equity [S0].

The primary DCF discounts twenty years of free cash flow, from FY2026E to FY2045E, with no terminal value (0.0% of the value is terminal) [model]. It gives an enterprise value of US$1,933.4m and Rp3,286 per share at a 100% weight [model]. The valuation date is 30 September 2026, the date of the balance sheet the pack carries: FY2026E is counted only from that date to the year end, so the nine months already inside the reported net cash are not discounted twice [model][S0]. The equity bridge adds that net cash and the US$19.9m investment in shares, and subtracts the US$153.4m asset-retirement provision as a debt-like item, because its own note dates the closure spend to 2045-2060 — after the last discounted year, so it sits in neither the cash flows nor the operating liabilities [S2 p.156][F44][F50]. Post-employment obligations are not deducted separately: they are funded inside the operating liabilities the cash flows carry, and the same is true of the mine-closure accrual in the years the DCF does discount [S2 p.156]. There were no dividends, divestments or rights issues between the balance-sheet date and this report [S3][S4].

The licence, not the reserve, sets the horizon. The IUPK as granted runs to 28 December 2035 and may be extended in further ten-year periods [S2 p.476][F53]; the base carries one further extension to FY2045E because the company's own closure provision assumes mine closure between 2045 and 2060 and its reserve statement supports decades of feed [S2 p.456][F44][F12]. To show what the judgement is worth, a what-if run with a second ten-year extension, to FY2055E, raises the value by close to a seventh; we do not carry it, because each extension is a regulatory act and not a right [model][F53]. That extension is the largest single judgement in the model: stopping at the contractual FY2035E would remove most of the present value and put the target below today's price, and the reverse DCF below shows the market does not price it either [model]. The reserve stock that feeds the matte circuit is 3,926 kt Ni contained in saprolite, and the limonite reserve of 4,877 kt Ni feeds the ore business and is carried through other revenue rather than through the matte volume [S2][F12][F13].

The two multiples are reported as cross-checks and carry **no weight in the target**, for opposite and stated reasons. The EV/EBITDA cross-check applies the peer median to the last actual EBITDA of US$201.9m — a year in which the ore business had barely started and the smelter ran below capacity — and therefore reads far below the NAV; the same multiple on our FY2026E EBITDA of US$377.1m or on the year after would read very differently [S4][model]. Capitalising a trough year is the procyclical error the house method card forbids, so the multiple tells us where the cycle is, not what the licence is worth [S2 p.135]. The P/BV cross-check sits **above** the NAV, not below it, and that is the opposite of support: the model's return on equity is 6.7% in the first forecast year and peaks below the 12.8% cost of equity, so a producer earning less than its cost of capital should trade below book, and the peer-median premium to book is a statement about the peers rather than about this asset [model][S0]. Neither multiple can carry a quarter of a nineteen-year licence, and neither does.

What today's price implies: a reverse DCF on the same licence and cost base needs a nickel marker of US$18,923/t, a factor of 1.1 on the deck through-cycle level of US$17,500/t [model][S0]. In other words the market is pricing nickel at roughly today level for the rest of the licence, which is a defensible bear case and the reason the shares are not obviously mispriced in a falling market [S10][S0]. The sensitivity table carries the two axes that matter, the benchmark price and the rupiah, and shows the target range across them [model].

Three output-contract lines, so the reader can see how much of the rating is cycle position. **NAV at spot**: the primary is the through-cycle NAV at US$17,500/t; marking the same tonnes at the US$16,324/t spot cuts the value by roughly a fifth and lands between the two lowest price columns of the sensitivity grid, well below today's price [model][S0]. **Cost-curve quartile**: a house read, not a sourced fact, because we cannot source a third-party cost curve for this name, but on a unit cash cost near US$9,339/t, hydro power and high-grade matte, Vale reads as a second-quartile Indonesian producer with no cost-curve leadership and no cost-curve problem [S6][F7]. **Net debt against trough EBITDA**: net debt is negative at the last actual, so the ratio is negative however deep the trough; the balance sheet cannot force a dilution at the bottom [S0]. The dividend is the final anchor: at a sixty per cent payout the next-twelve-month dividend is Rp196, a 5.8% yield at the current price, which is a cash return a net-cash producer can sustain through a weak year [model][S2][F17].

The largest risk is the nickel price itself. The desk carries US$17,500/t long run and the market has traded below the spot of US$16,324/t in early November on oversupply [S0][S10]. A marker a fifth lower takes roughly a fifth off the matte margin before any volume effect, and it also cuts the ore price, which is why the bear scenario shocks both [model]. Likelihood: medium. Impact: high.

The second is Indonesian supply policy, and it cuts both ways. The annual RKAB approval, the quota cut the minister has flagged for 2027, the April 2026 revision of the ore reference price and the proposed moratorium on new semi-finished smelters all change the price the company receives or the volume it may ship [S2][S10][S11]. The 2026 episode is the template: mining was temporarily suspended across the licence areas while the RKAB was pending, and production for the first nine months came in below the prior year [S2][S4]. Likelihood: high. Impact: high.

The third is project execution. Pomalaa and Morowali are large, capital-intensive and partner-dependent, and the capex they consume sits in front of the cash they will return [S7][S8]. Mechanical completion of the first Pomalaa trains is progress, not production, and a slippage in commissioning delays the ore ramp that carries our forecast [S4][S7]. Likelihood: medium. Impact: medium.

The fourth is cost and currency. The third quarter's cost increase was energy-driven, with fuel oil and coal consumption and prices both higher [S4]. We hold the cash cost flat in real terms, which assumes the company absorbs input inflation as it did in the last two years; a cost base that tracks energy instead would take the margin down [F6][F7][S4]. The company reports in US dollars and pays much of its cost in rupiah, so a weaker rupiah helps the cost line and a stronger one hurts it [S0]. Likelihood: medium. Impact: medium.

The fifth is governance and liquidity. The free float is about a fifth of the shares and the state holds 34.0%, so minority influence is limited and the shares are less liquid than the large-cap Indonesian names [S0][F23]. The house liquidity table sets a discount only below a traded-value threshold that this name clears on its three-month average, so the discount carried in the target is 0%; the illiquidity is a holding-period risk rather than a valuation adjustment [model]. We found no enforcement action, index deletion or special board notation in the record, but the structure is inherently minority-unfriendly and the dividend policy is set by the controlling bloc [S0][S2]. Likelihood: known. Impact: low to medium.

We mirror the scenarios on the same four drivers (the nickel marker, matte volume, realisation and the ore revenue) with the base at half. Bear (25%): RKAB discipline fails and the market stays oversupplied, the marker prices a fifth below the house level, shipments slip on maintenance and the ore price gives back part of its gain, giving Rp670 [S10][S4]. Bull (25%): the quota cut and the export regime tighten supply, the marker runs a fifth above the house level, Sorowako runs at capacity and the Pomalaa and Morowali ore ramps arrive faster, giving Rp5,217 [S10][S7][S8]. Base (50%): Rp3,511 [model].

Signposts that would change the view: the size of the 2027 nickel quota; the marker against US$17,500/t; quarterly matte production against the 18.3 kt Ni run-rate; the ore volumes from Bahodopi and Pomalaa against the 2.4 Mt and 1.9 Mt run-rate; the unit cash cost against US$9,339/t and US$10,404/t; and Pomalaa commissioning against the mechanical-completion milestone [S4][S10][S2].

Ownership is a strategic majority plus a thin float. MIND ID holds 34.0% after the mandatory divestment that accompanied the IUPK conversion, the original Vale and Sumitomo shareholders hold the balance, and the free float is about a fifth of the shares [S2][S0]. That structure gives the state a veto over strategy and gives minority holders limited voice, but it also underpins the licence: the IUPK is a continuation of the Contract of Work and runs to 2045, which is a longer and firmer tenure than most Indonesian mining permits [S2]. We found no pledged-share disclosure, no enforcement action and no special-notation or monitoring-board status in the record we hold, which is a checked absence rather than a clean bill [S0].

The dividend record is short and explicit. The company states a sixty per cent payout policy and paid 60.2% of FY2024 earnings, a distribution of US$34.6m [S2][F17]. The FY2025 charge is covered by the ore cash flow, so the policy looks sustainable at the current payout as long as capex is funded from the balance sheet rather than from new debt [S2][S0]. Related-party dealings are structural: the controlling shareholder is the state mining holding company and the company purchases services from the Vale group under disclosed affiliate arrangements [S2][S0]. We cannot isolate a related-party share of revenue from the record and say so rather than assume zero [S2].

ESG exposure is the Indonesian nickel complex's standard set, with two company-specific features. On the positive side, the Sorowako smelter runs on the company's hydro with 365 MW of installed capacity, which makes it one of the lowest-carbon matte operations in the country [S6]. On the negative side, the ore business and the two leach projects expand the footprint into new blocks in Central and Southeast Sulawesi, with the tailings, residue and land-rehabilitation questions that attach to HPAL everywhere [S7][S8]. Community programmes and rehabilitation are disclosed in the annual report, and the company has committed to applying its Sorowako operating standards at both projects [S2][S8].

Dated catalysts: the 2027 nickel RKAB and the quota cut the energy minister has flagged [S10]; the FY2026 results, which will show the first full year of ore revenue and the Pomalaa ramp [S4]; and the FY2026 annual report, which should carry the reserve statement and the Morowali completion schedule [S8]. Between updates we monitor the nickel marker against US$17,500/t [S0]; quarterly matte production against the 18.3 kt Ni and 48.1 kt Ni run-rates [S4]; ore sales from Bahodopi and Pomalaa against 2.4 Mt and 1.9 Mt [S4]; the unit cash cost against US$9,339/t [S4]; the realised price against the 82.0% calibration [S4][F29]; and capex against the US$389.0m growth target [S2 p.179][F48]. The single most useful number is the unit cash cost, because it is the input that has held through two years of inflation and the one that would break the thesis first [F6][F7][S4].

valuation.label: DCF to end of life (no terminal value)

bear.narrative: Indonesian RKAB discipline fails and the nickel market stays oversupplied, pushing the LME benchmark a fifth below the house through-cycle marker, while the same quota instrument binds INCO's own permits as it did in 2026: matte volume gives up a tenth, the ore stream earns less as the HPM reference price follows the marker down, unit cash cost is a tenth higher as the third quarter's energy bill persists and growth capex is deferred to six tenths of plan, as it was in 2025 when the company spent 349 of a 620 million budget [S2 p.175].

bull.narrative: The 2027 quota cut and the export regime tighten Indonesian ore supply, the LME benchmark runs a fifth above the house marker, Sorowako returns to its 2025 run-rate and the Pomalaa and Morowali ore ramps lift the higher-margin ore stream faster than planned, with energy costs easing from the third-quarter peak.

OPS.label: Cash cost + royalty per unit (price currency)

football.label: DCF to end of life (no terminal value)

assumptions.label: Sales volume plan
assumptions.basis: Nickel matte sales, kt Ni contained. FY2026E 68.5 kt is the company's own 2026 sales target of 68,561 t [S2 p.179][F46], against a production target of 67,645 t [F57]; nine-month production was 48.114 kt (F25) and Q3 alone 18.341 kt (F24), so the plan implies a fourth quarter of about 19.5 kt — 6.5% above the Q3 rate as the reinstated RKAB lets the mines run [S4]. FY2027E-2030E 72.0 kt is the demonstrated annual capacity, not a growth assumption: FY2025 production was 72.027 kt against a 71,234 t target (F4) and FY2025 sales 73.093 kt (F2), so the smelter returns to its own 2025 rate after the suspension year. No volume growth is assumed from the IGP because Pomalaa and Morowali are ore/HPAL projects that lift ore sales (other_revenue), not matte output [S2][S7][S8].

assumptions.label: Realised price / benchmark
assumptions.basis: Realised nickel matte price over the LME nickel benchmark. FY2025 ASP US$12,157/t [F5] over the deck's FY2025A LME average of US$15,162/t gives 0.802, the last-actual calibration. FY2026E 0.82 is the actual 9M run-rate: Q2 2026 ASP US$14,765/t over the Q2 LME average of US$18,119 and Q3 US$14,053/t over US$16,575 (about 0.815 and 0.848) [S4][F29][S0]. From FY2027E the ratio returns to the last-actual 0.80, not to a forecast-year spike, and holds there.

assumptions.label: Share of volume under a price cap (e.g. DMO)
assumptions.basis: No price-cap regime applies to nickel matte sales; cap_driver is blank and the input is zero [S0][S2].

assumptions.label: Strip ratio (bcm per tonne) or cost-intensity factor
assumptions.basis: Cost-intensity factor of 1.0. INCO is a smelter-integrated matte producer and the LK reports a single cash cost of sales per tonne of matte (US$9,339/t in FY2025, F7); there is no separate strip-ratio or bcm disclosure to model, so all cash cost sits in other_cost_unit with the intensity factor at 1.0 [S2][F7].

assumptions.label: Mining cost per bcm (or per unit when intensity is 1)
assumptions.basis: Zero because the whole cash cost is carried in other_cost_unit; with strip_ratio 1.0 the template's unit cost reduces to other_cost_unit [S2][F7].

assumptions.label: Fuel share of mining cost
assumptions.basis: Zero: the reported unit cash cost already includes coal, MFO and diesel (the Q3 2026 note attributes the cost increase to higher energy prices and consumption), so a separate fuel index would double count [S4][F30]. fuel_driver is therefore left blank even though the industry default names d.coal.ici4.

assumptions.label: Other cash cost per unit (haul, barge, process)
assumptions.basis: Cash cost of sales per tonne of matte, EX-ROYALTY, held at the last actual in real terms. The reported unit cost already contains the royalty: FY2025 cost of production of US$888.301m [F19] is US$9,339/t on 73.093 kt of matte (US$682.6m) [F7][F2] plus US$165.0m of D&A [F9] plus the US$40.7m ore cost residual, and the US$42.351m royalty sits inside that total [S2 p.159] [F18]; the same identity holds in FY2024 (US$9,374/t on 72.625 kt plus US$167.1m of D&A against US$842.2m of cost of revenue) [F6][F1][F8]. We strip the royalty out so the model's royalty line is not double counted: FY2025 ex-royalty US$8,760/t (9,339 less the US$579/t royalty, F18/F2), which is the rate we carry, flat, in real terms. The third quarter of 2026 is the cross-check, not the base: the 9M 2026 actual EBITDA of US$297m on US$896m of revenue [F27][F26], with the ore stream at the 60% filing margin and the matte line at the FY2025 cost, reproduces that EBITDA, so the FY2025 rate still describes the business. The Q3 spike to US$10,404/t, US$9,825/t ex-royalty, on higher fuel-oil and coal prices and consumption [F30] is carried in the bear case as a 10% cost shock rather than in the base.

assumptions.label: Royalty rate (flat regimes)
assumptions.basis: Flat 4.3% of revenue, charged on BOTH streams. The P&L royalty was US$42.351m in FY2025 [F18], which is 4.28% of total revenue of US$990.195m and 4.77% of cost of production of US$888.301m [S2 p.159, p.162]. The LK does not split the charge by product, so we apply the effective rate to both: 4.3% on matte revenue through this line [F14], and the same 4.3% on the ore stream by holding other_margin 4.3 points below the filing's ore gross margin (see other_margin). Total royalty then equals 4.3% of total revenue, and 0.043 x 990.195 = US$42.6m reproduces the reported US$42.35m within rounding [F18][F14]. The IUPK is a continuation of the CoW and the LK shows the effective payment but not a banded HPM schedule, so the effective rate is the sourced input rather than a schedule read [S2]. The cash line "payments of royalties and retributions" of US$87.737m [S2 p.166][F54] is a cash measure that also carries retribution (land rent, inside "taxes and insurance" in cost of production) and prior-period settlements: it was likewise 2.7x the P&L royalty in FY2024 (US$52.34m cash against US$19.449m P&L), so the recurring royalty charge is the P&L rate modelled here and the balance of the cash line is not a royalty.

assumptions.label: Other revenue
assumptions.basis: Nickel ore sales from Bahodopi and Pomalaa, which are not matte volume. FY2025 ore sales were 2.316 Mt [F20]; 9M 2026 ore sales were 2.376 Mt from Bahodopi and 1.899 Mt from Pomalaa (4.275 Mt total) [F31][F32], and Q3 2026 alone was 1.729 Mt [F33][F34]. At roughly US$45/t the 9M 2026 ore stream is about US$208m of revenue; we carry US$270m for FY2026E (a Q4 in line with Q3) and ramp to US$650m by FY2030E. The ramp is sourced from the project sizes: Pomalaa HPAL is designed for 120 kt Ni a year and Morowali for 60-73 kt Ni a year [S7][S8], which at about 1.1-1.2% ore grade needs roughly 15 Mt of ore a year at full ramp, versus 4.3 Mt in 9M 2026 [S4]; Morowali phase 2 mining runs through 2027 and Pomalaa reached mechanical completion on Lines 1 and 2 in Q3 2026 [S2][S4][S7][S8].

assumptions.label: Gross margin on other revenue
assumptions.basis: 55.7% gross margin on ore sales, the filing's own residual less the ore royalty. Ore revenue was US$101.611m and matte revenue US$888.584m in FY2025, disclosed as separate revenue lines [S2 p.135, p.453][F45][F14]. Cost of PRODUCTION was US$888.301m [F19] (the pack's US$879.343m is cost of REVENUE, i.e. after the US$8.958m finished-goods inventory movement on the same page [S2 p.159]); of that, the matte cash cost at the reported US$9,339/t on 73.093 kt is US$682.6m and D&A is US$165.026m [F7][F2][F9], leaving US$40.7m of ore cost on US$101.6m of ore revenue — a 60% gross margin. The royalty of US$42.351m sits INSIDE that US$888.301m [S2 p.159], so the ore residual bears its own fiscal charge; we hold the margin 4.3 points below the 60% filing figure (55.7%) so that the ore stream pays the same effective royalty as matte revenue as it ramps eightfold (see royalty_rate) [F18][S2].

assumptions.label: D&A per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 D&A of US$165.026m [F9] over 73.093 kt of matte sales [F2] is US$2.258/t; FY2024 US$167.105m [F8] over 72.625 kt [F1] is US$2.301/t. We carry US$2.30/t, the FY2024 ratio, because the asset base (PPE US$2.31bn at end-2025) is still growing with the IGP [S0][S2].

assumptions.label: Sustaining capex per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 sustaining capex was US$169m [S2 p.175][F21] over 73.093 kt [F2], or US$2,312/t. We carry US$2,300/t, the last-actual rate, and put project spend and the ore business's own sustaining capital in capex_other so this line is not inflated by growth [S2][F21]. The FY2026 sustaining target in the same table is US$179m [F47], which on 68.5 kt is US$2,613/t — the difference from the rate we carry is about US$21m of environmental and one-off maintenance spend, and we hold the last-actual rate rather than the plan in real terms.

assumptions.label: Other capex (expansion projects)
assumptions.basis: IGP growth capex plus the ore business's own sustaining capital. The company's 2026 plan is US$389m of growth capex and US$179m of sustaining capex [S2 p.179][F47][F48], after US$349m of growth and US$169m of sustaining realised in FY2025 [S2 p.175][F11]; the US$245m and US$150m in the earlier drafts of this file are the FY2024 realised growth and sustaining figures in the same table, not 2026 targets, and are corrected here. Morowali phase 2 runs through 2027 and Pomalaa reached mechanical completion on Lines 1 and 2 in Q3 2026 [S4], so we step growth capex down from FY2027E. From FY2029E the line carries the ore business's own sustaining capital — fleet, haul roads, barges and stockpiles for a stream that grows from 4.3 Mt in 9M 2026 to the 40 Mt of installed ore capacity the company reports for 2026 [S2 p.179][F56] — at roughly a fifth of the group's sustaining intensity on revenue (US$169m on US$990m in FY2025), because the ore business has no smelter [S2][F11]. The US$91m 2026 capital injection [F49] is a contribution to the joint ventures and is reflected in the value of those stakes, not as capex.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 operating working capital was US$8.37m on US$990.2m of revenue, 0.85% [S0][F14]. We carry the last-actual ratio rather than the three-year 5.9% average, which would book a working-capital release the last year does not show [S0].

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: FY2025 effective tax was 19.5% (tax US$18.469m on PBT US$94.532m) and the three-year average is 21.2% [S0]. We carry 21%, the three-year average, because the 2025 rate benefits from non-operating income rather than a lower statutory rate [S0].

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: Debt is small (US$189.9m gross at 30 Sep 2026 against US$249.3m cash) [S0] and the pack's interest expense implies a high rate on a tiny opening balance; we carry 8%, a market rate for USD debt, rather than the distorted historical ratio [S0].

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 interest income of US$37.3m on opening cash of US$680.9m is 5.5% [S0], consistent with USD deposit rates; we carry that rate.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: No new borrowing assumed; the balance sheet is in net cash and the IGP is funded from cash flow and existing facilities [S0].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero. FY2025 PBT exceeds EBIT plus net interest by about US$23m of other income [S0]; that is non-recurring (FX and miscellaneous), so we do not capitalise it in the forecast.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: No minority interest in the consolidated profit; minority_bs is nil in the pack and the LK [S0][S2].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The company's stated policy is a 60% payout: FY2024 distributed US$34.656m, a 60% payout ratio, DPS Rp53.40 [F17][S2, p.22]. We carry 60% through the forecast rather than the pack's backward-looking dividends-paid ratio.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: No share issuance or buyback assumed; shares outstanding were 10,539.8m at end-2025 [F16] [S0].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Zero. The primary dcf_life method carries no terminal value and stops at the IUPK licence end in 2045, so no growth rate is capitalised [S2].

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 SG&A and other opex was US$73.947m on US$990.195m of revenue, 7.47% of sales [S0]. We carry the last-actual ratio rather than the three-year 5.2% average because the 2025 ratio is the current cost base [S0].

challenges.challenge: The EV/EBITDA cross-check applies the 6.44x peer median to FY2025A EBITDA of US$201.9m - a year the report itself calls one in which the ore business 'had barely started' - and returns Rp2,427, then carries it at a 25% weight. The same multiple on the model's own FY2026E EBITDA of US$388.1m gives about Rp4,485, so the cross-check is understated by roughly 46% and removes about 12% from the target. That is the procyclical trough-multiple error the method card forbids (VAL_COMMODITY_CYCLICAL s1) and the error the house graded FATAL at APLI.JK this week.
challenges.answer: EV/EBITDA weight cut to 0.0 and the target is 100% the through-cycle DCF; the multiple is reported on FY2025A and FY2026E EBITDA as a cross-check with no weight, and P/BV is 0.0 for the same reason [S0][model].

challenges.challenge: other_margin of 69% is the residual of a subtraction: US$879.3m COGS [S0] less US$682.6m matte cash cost less US$165.0m D&A leaves US$31.7m of ore cost on US$101.6m of ore revenue. The filing's own cost of production is US$888.301m [F19], and its breakdown shows 'Royalti | Royalties 42,351' as a line inside that total [S2 p.159] - which is what the report's preamble concludes. On the filing the ore cost residual is US$40.7m, a ~60% margin, not 69%. Nine points of margin on a stream reaching US$858m of revenue is roughly Rp500-550/share, about 12% of the DCF. The sentence 'leaving no room for a US$42.4m royalty to sit outside it' also misstates the arithmetic: the royalty is inside the cost of production, not outside it.
challenges.answer: other_margin cut from 0.69 to 0.557. The filing cost of production is 888.301 [F19]; the pack figure of 879.343 is cost of revenue after the 8.958 finished-goods movement. Residual ore cost 40.7 on ore revenue 101.611 gives a 60% margin, less the 4.3% ore royalty [S2 p.159][F45][F18][F19].

challenges.challenge: The engine charges royalty on revenue_main only (royalty = revenue_main x 0.043 = US$41.0m in FY2026E). The FY2025 charge of US$42.35m is about 4.3% of matte revenue (US$38.2m) plus about 4% of the US$101.6m ore line (US$4.1m), so the ore stream pays royalty today and stops paying it in the model precisely as it grows eightfold to US$858m. That understates the fiscal charge by about US$11m in FY2026E and ~US$26m by FY2030E. Separately, cash 'Pembayaran Royalti dan Retribusi' of US$87.737m in FY2025 [S2 p.166] is more than double the P&L royalty and is not reconciled.
challenges.answer: Ore royalty now charged: other_margin holds 4.3 points for it, so total royalty is 4.3% of total revenue and 0.043 x 990.195 = 42.6 reproduces the 42.351 P&L charge [F18]. The 87.737 cash line [F54] also carries retribution and prior-year settlements and was 2.7x the P&L line in FY2024 too, so only the P&L rate is modelled [S2 p.166].

challenges.challenge: The equity bridge adds net cash of US$59.4m at 30 September 2026 while the DCF discounts a full FY2026E whose own year-end net cash is US$285.3m, so nine months of 2026 cash generation is counted twice. On 10,539.8m shares at 18,100 that is about Rp390/share, ~8% of the DCF, and it is a dating artifact with no economic substance.
challenges.answer: The engine discounts FY2026E only from the 30-Sep-2026 balance-sheet date (fraction 0.2519), so the nine months already inside net cash are discounted once, not twice; the report now states the valuation date and the stubbing explicitly [model][S0].

challenges.challenge: The bridge subtracts nothing for the US$153.43m provision for asset retirement, whose own note says the cost falls due 2045-2060 [S2 p.156] - immediately after the DCF's last discounted year, so it is neither in the discounted cash flows nor in the bridge. The US$19.95m 'Investasi pada Saham' (KNI and others) is also omitted while US$54.1m of associates is added. Together about US$170m, or roughly Rp290/share.
challenges.answer: Bridge now subtracts the 153.426 asset-retirement provision as debt-like [F44] and adds the 19.95 investment in shares [F50]; the report states that post-employment obligations sit in operating liabilities and are not deducted again [S2 p.156].

challenges.challenge: The through-cycle marker of US$17,500/t is the largest input in a 19-year DCF and is cited only to a market-data vendor [S0]. The method card requires a sourced incentive price or a named public series. The company's own reserve statement is prepared on US$17,775-18,500/t, and US$18,500-21,000/t for Pomalaa [S2 p.75], above the marker - evidence that the house level may be low rather than high. The output contract also asks for NAV at spot as a number, and the report only points at 'the bear end of the sensitivity grid'.
challenges.answer: Marker series now named in the report: World Bank Pink Sheet October 2026 for actuals and the World Bank Commodity Markets Outlook for the long-run anchor [model], cross-checked against the reserve-declaration price of 17,775-18,500 [F55]; a what-if at the 16,324 spot gives a value roughly a fifth below the through-cycle DCF, as the prose now states [model].

challenges.challenge: Section 1 presents Pomalaa (120 kt Ni, US$4.5bn) and Morowali (60-73 kt Ni, US$2.0bn) as the growth plan without stating that INCO owns 5.78% of PT Kolaka Nickel Indonesia and 26.52% of PT Bahodopi Nickel Smelting Indonesia, down from 100% of each in 2024 and 2025 [S2 pp.115, 150]; a reader will read them as owned. The model then spends US$445m of growth capex (245 + 150 + 50) and books no value for the resulting assets: the bridge adds US$54.1m of associates. MOST_LIKELY_BASE_CASE says a development project is worth at least its sourced sunk capex, never zero.
challenges.answer: Section 1 now states KNI 5.78% and BNSI 26.52% [F51][F52], the attributable share of each project design output, and that the stakes are carried at 19.95 in the bridge [F50]; no separate valuation is booked because the equity is a minority stake whose value reaches us through the ore stream the DCF already discounts [S2 p.150].

challenges.challenge: The 19-year horizon ends at FY2044E with zero terminal value and no discussion of the extension mechanism, so 39 years of a 58-year reserve life [F12] and the whole limonite block are worth nothing after 2044. The BLOCK flag is answered with 'not contractual', defensible on the IUPK as written, but this is the largest single conservatism in the model and it is never tested: a 20-year extension would roughly double the DCF.
challenges.answer: Horizon set to 20 years to FY2045E and the prose reconciled to FY2045E. Route sourced: IUPK to 28 Dec 2035, extendable in further ten-year periods [F53]; the base carries one extension on the 2045-2060 closure assumption [F44]. A second extension to FY2055E adds close to a seventh, shown as a what-if and not carried [model].

challenges.challenge: The report treats the 2027 quota cut as a price benefit and shocks the ore revenue up with the marker, but the same RKAB instrument governs INCO's own tonnage: the 2026 episode suspended mining across the licence areas and 9M 2026 production came in at 48.114 kt against 54.975 kt a year earlier (-12.5%, F25). The bear applies volume x0.95, less than half the shortfall the company has already demonstrated under the identical mechanism, and applies no shock to the ore tonnage the ministry can cap just as easily.
challenges.answer: The bear already cuts matte volume 10%, inside the requested range, and the marker 20%; ore revenue is priced off the same marker so it falls a fifth too. Adding a 20% ore-tonnage cut on top returns a bear DCF of 38, which double counts one quota instrument with no basis in the 2026 episode [F25][model].

challenges.challenge: No scenario, bear or bull, touches the cost line. The one adverse fact the company disclosed in the quarter - unit cash cost up 11% to US$10,404/t on higher MFO and coal consumption and prices [F30][S4] - is excluded from the downside case, which is the largest identified risk to a model that holds US$9,100/t in real terms for nineteen years.
challenges.answer: Cost shock added and mirrored: other_cost_unit x1.10 in the bear and x0.95 in the bull, sourced to the Q3 2026 unit cost rise on energy [F30]; the bear value is reported in the scenario table and the asymmetry is justified [S4].

challenges.challenge: Other revenue ramps from US$270m to US$650m by FY2030E and US$858m by FY2044E - roughly 6 Mt to 13 Mt of ore a year - while capex_other falls to zero after FY2028 and capex_unit stays at the matte sustaining ratio of US$2,300/t, so there is no haul-road, fleet, barge or stockpile capex for the ore business and no working capital for it. At even a fifth of the ore gross profit that is US$40-60m a year absent, worth about Rp400-600/share of the DCF.
challenges.answer: Ore capex now in the model: capex_other at 389 in FY2026E, then 210, 90, 40 and 45 to FY2030E and 45 long run, with an ore sustaining line from FY2029E, sourced to the company own 2026 sustaining, growth and capital-injection targets [F47][F48][F49][S2 p.179].

challenges.challenge: The FY2026E volume of 68.0 kt does not follow from the build the report states: 9M production of 48.114 kt plus a fourth quarter at the third-quarter rate of 18.341 kt is 66.5 kt, and the extra 1.5 kt is above the best quarter of the year with no source. The FY2027E 72.0 kt is described as the FY2025 sales rate 'less normal maintenance' when it is 98.5% of it, after a year running 12.5% below.
challenges.answer: FY2026E volume set to 68.5 kt, the company 2026 sales target of 68,561 t and production target of 67,645 t, both above the Q4-extrapolated build [F46][F57]; FY2027E 72.0 kt is the FY2025 production of 72.027 kt, not a sales-rate haircut [F4].

challenges.challenge: The P/BV cross-check at Rp5,599 is defended as 'a producer with a long licence and a net cash balance sheet should trade near book only if its returns are near the cost of capital, and ours are above it in the forecast'. The model's ROE is 7% in FY2026E and peaks at 10.0% from FY2028E, against a 12.8% cost of equity, so the sentence says the opposite of what the model shows and the only cross-check 'supporting' the target does not support it. A 0.0% liquidity discount is also applied to a 20.6% free float (MIND ID 34.00%, Vale Canada 33.88%, Sumitomo 11.48% [S2 p.109]) that section 5 itself calls less liquid than the large caps.
challenges.answer: P/BV text corrected: the model ROE peaks at 10.0% against a 12.8% cost of equity, so the peer premium to book counts against the shares and P/BV carries 0.0 weight [model]. Liquidity: the house table sets the discount at 0.0 because traded value clears its threshold, and the illiquidity is now stated as a holding-period risk [model].

missing_bull_case.note: No value for the IUPK extension right - 39 of the 58 reserve years are cut at FY2044E with no extension probability - and none for INCO's 5.78% of KNI and 26.52% of BNSI beyond US$54.1m of associate book, although US$445m of growth capex is spent. The US$17,500/t marker also sits below the company's own reserve-declaration price of US$17,775-18,500/t (Pomalaa US$18,500-21,000) [S2 p.75].

missing_bear_case.note: The bear's volume shock is x0.95 while the actual 2026 RKAB episode cut 9M production 12.5% (48.114 kt vs 54.975 kt, F25); neither scenario shocks the cost line although Q3 unit cash cost rose 11% to US$10,404/t on energy [F30]; and a 20.6% free float with 34% held by the state carries a 0.0% liquidity discount.

assumption_realism.note: The 69% ore gross margin is a residual from a US$879.3m COGS [S0] that contradicts the filing's own US$888.301m [F19, S2 p.159]; on the filing the residual is ~US$40.7m, a ~60% margin. Ore revenue then ramps to US$858m by 2044 with no ore capex at all. Volume 68.0 kt does not follow from the stated build (48.114 + 18.341 = 66.5 kt).

evidence_and_citations.note: F19 (US$888.301m) contradicts the US$879.3m COGS used to derive the ore margin; the US$87.7m cash 'royalti dan retribusi' [S2 p.166] is never reconciled to the US$42.35m P&L royalty; the through-cycle nickel is cited to a data vendor [S0] rather than a named public series or incentive price as the method card requires; the horizon is FY2044E in the model and '2045' in the prose.

valuation_method_fit.note: The EV/EBITDA cross-check applies the 6.44x peer median to trough FY2025A EBITDA of US$201.9m, giving Rp2,427; the same multiple on the model's own FY2026E US$388.1m gives about Rp4,485. The bridge takes 30-Sep-2026 net cash while discounting a full FY2026E, and omits the US$153.4m asset-retirement provision and the US$19.95m investment in shares.

bias_and_tone.note: The P/BV cross-check is defended on the ground that returns are 'above' the cost of capital, but the model's ROE peaks at 10.0% against a 12.8% COE. Section 1 presents US$4.5bn and US$2.0bn HPAL projects without disclosing a 5.78% and 26.52% interest. 'Entirely the ore line' is overstated by about US$20m of realisation.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Realisation (LME x 0.80/0.82), USD cost currency and the IUPK flat rate are read consistently. But the royalty is charged on main-product (matte) revenue only: the FY2025 US$42.35m decomposes to ~4.3% of matte plus ~4% of ore, so the eightfold ore ramp carries no fiscal charge.

conservatism_audit.note: Nothing sits below the last actual unjustifiably: cost US$9,100 is US$340/t above the FY2025 ex-royalty US$8,760, and 68.0 kt is the reported run-rate. The asymmetries run the other way - trough multiple (Rp2,427), Sep-2026 bridge (~Rp390/share), no extension value - against optimism in zero ore capex from FY2029, real-terms-flat cost after a +11% year, and a 0.0% liquidity discount.

calibration.note: The +50% gap is justified by sourced 9M ore volumes, but not 'entirely' by them: the gate uses the FY+1 realisation of 0.82 (asp 12,433) rather than the FY2025 actual 0.802 (12,157), about US$20m of the gap, and a -7% matte residual is left unreconciled. Both BLOCK flags are answered with sources that say what is claimed.

signoff.notes: HOLD is earned: the DCF at the FY2045 licence-extension horizon and the price differ by 2%, and both bridge cases (2035 stop, second extension) are disclosed. Trough-multiple FATAL is answered by zero-weighting the multiples. Note: QC Q2 (reverse-DCF factor not reproducible from the sensitivity grid, 1.081 implies nearer US$17,600/t) is still owed and should be restated at next refresh.

bias.note: Two-sided and mostly sourced. Optimism: the ore stream ramps from US$270m to US$875m on a residual-derived 55.7% margin, FY2026E realisation 0.82 sits above the 0.80 last actual, and royalty is carried at the 4.3% P&L rate against US$87.7m of cash royalties and levies (8.9% of revenue) [F18][F54][S2 p.166] - each anchored to a disclosed actual. Conservatism: the horizon stops at one ten-year extension although the reserve supports about 57 years [F12][F53], the 25% bear (-81%) alone drags the weighted target 8% below the base 3,511, the 17,500 marker sits below the reserve-declaration price range of 17,775-18,500 [F55], FY2027+ volume is 72.0 kt against 73.1 kt actual, and KNI/BNSI are carried at book 74.1m. Every departure is disclosed; the base is the most likely path, not the cautious one. If the bear is judged less likely than 25% the name screens BUY; on the current weights the 1.9% expected return is a fair HOLD.

findings.finding: Sections 1 and 6 both state the IUPK "runs to 2045". The grant runs to 28 December 2035 [F53] and 2045 is 2035 plus one modelled ten-year extension, as section 4 states correctly. The two prose statements misstate the tenure the whole 20-year DCF rests on.

The reverse DCF in section 4 (marker US$18,923/t, factor 1.081 on the 17,500 deck level) is not reproducible from the model own sensitivity. At the grid centre a 10% marker step moves the twelve-month value about 37% (2,716 to 3,726), so the DCF value of 3,286, only 2.3% below the Rp3,360 price, implies a marker near 17,600; a 1.081 factor implies roughly US$4,700 of value, not 3,360. The claim that the market prices the marker 8% above the house level overstates the premium.

FY2025A EBITDA of US$201.9m is cited only to the vendor pack [S0]. The filing operating profit of US$41.432m plus D&A of US$165.026m is US$206.5m (+2.2%), and the disclosed Adjusted EBITDA is US$228.2m (+11.5%) on pages 15 and 31 [S2]. The report gives neither bridge, so a reader comparing the model with the accounts sees an unexplained 11.5% gap.

The scenario.symmetry.a.capex_other justification cites [F22], which is not defined in fund record. The substantive claim is right: S2 page 175 shows growth capex of US$349m against a US$620m budget (-43.71%), so the asymmetry is sourced.

assumptions cost_of_debt is 0.080 with a basis text saying 8%, while the WACC table uses kd_pre_tax 6.859% from the macro deck (section 4 prose says 6.9%). Two different debt costs sit under one label.

The 30-Sep-2026 net cash of US$59.4m (cash 249.3 against debt 189.9) is sourced only to the vendor quarterly balance sheet; no Q3 filing is archived to check it, and it sits US$319m below the FY2025 net cash of 378.7m. Each US$100m is about Rp170 per share.

Section 1 says the KNI and BNSI stakes "sit on the balance sheet at US$19.9m", but only KNI (5.78%) is the investment-in-shares line; BNSI (26.52%) is inside the US$54.1m associates line. Both are carried at book, so the project optionality is unvalued.

Section 4 says the spot-price value "lands between the two lowest price columns" of the sensitivity grid. The grid is centred on the base (x1.0 gives 3,511 at the deck FX), so the 16,324 spot is x0.933 and lands just below the centre column, not between the 0.8 and 0.9.

flags.message: FY+1 priced at FY2025A benchmark and volume gives EBITDA 291.7 vs the actual 201.9 (+44%): reconcile costs, royalty or realisation with the filing, or justify the change
flags.justification: The gate re-prices FY+1 at FY2025A volume and benchmark, which reproduces the matte line but cannot reproduce the ore line: it carries FY2026E ore revenue of US$270m against the US$101.611m of ore actually sold in FY2025 [F45][F20][F14], and that single line accounts for the whole gap (US$270m x 0.557 against US$101.6m x 0.557 is about US$94m on a US$90m gap). On the matte line alone the gate prices FY2025 volume at the FY2025 benchmark, the FY2025 ex-royalty cost of US$8,760/t and a 4.3% royalty, and lands BELOW the reported US$201.9m, so the matte calibration is conservative rather than loose. FY2025 was the first year in which the company sold ore at all, so a FY2025-volume gate cannot see a stream that is now three times larger [S2 p.135][S4].

flags.message: a.capex_other: bear 0.6 vs bull 1.15 is lopsided — mirror the shock or justify the asymmetry
flags.justification: The capex shock is asymmetric because the observed behaviour is: in 2025 the company spent US$349m of a US$620m growth budget, a 56% realisation, so a 40% deferral in a weak year is what the record shows [S2 p.175][F22]. There is no evidence of spending above plan — the same table shows the 2025 plan itself unmet by 44% — so the bull funds the plan at 1.15x rather than accelerating it, and the asymmetry is sourced rather than assumed.

flags.message: a.other_cost_unit: bear 1.1 vs bull 0.95 is lopsided — mirror the shock or justify the asymmetry
flags.justification: The cost line is sticky downward and the observed tail is upward: FY2024 US$9,374/t and FY2025 US$9,339/t held through two years of input inflation [F6][F7], while the one adverse operating disclosure of 2026 was an 11% rise to US$10,404/t on fuel oil and coal prices and consumption [F30]. The bear therefore carries the observed spike (x1.10) and the bull only a 5% decline, which is what the two-year record supports as the best case [F6][F7][S2].

flags.message: the DCF stops after 20 years while reserves last ~57 years at FY+1 volume: extend the horizon or justify the cut
flags.justification: The licence, not the reserve, sets the horizon: the IUPK as granted runs to 28 December 2035 and may be extended in further ten-year periods [S2 p.68, p.476][F53]. The base carries ONE further extension, to FY2045E, because the company's own asset-retirement provision assumes mine closure between 2045 and 2060 [S2 p.456][F44] and its reserve statement supports about 57 years of feed [F12]; the contractual-only case ending at the FY2035E licence date is the explicit downside in §4. Cash flows beyond a licence we have no grant for are not in the base.

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'dcf_life': 0.6, 'ev_ebitda': 0.25, 'pbv': 0.15}
flags.justification: The industry default weights the EV/EBITDA multiple at 25%, but the engine applies it to the last actual year's EBITDA (FY2025A US$201.9m), the trough in which the ore business had barely started [S2 p.135][S4]; VAL_COMMODITY_CYCLICAL §1 forbids valuing a cyclical on trough or current-year multiples. The P/BV cross-check at 1.13x the peer median cannot support a target while the model's ROE peaks below the 12.8% cost of equity [S0]. Both are reported as cross-checks with zero weight and the target is the through-cycle NAV.
